items.content:
The constellations are Greek by way of Babylon and maybe three thousand
years old, which is nothing. Other people looked at the same sky and drew
a different animal. And the stars *move* — slowly, but they do. So the
shapes have a start date and an end date.

Something about that is enormous and I can't say why yet.

summary: Greek star-shapes are recent, arbitrary, and slowly dissolving
title: Constellations aren't fixed
